unmapped_findings: The tabulated measured yield strength of AN750 is 709 MPa (Table 3), yet the engineering stress–strain curve for the 750 °C condition (Fig. 12, black) exhibits a long plateau slightly above 1000 MPa from ~13 % to 30 % strain ending near 33 % strain — the high plateau is the flow/UTS level while the reported YS (0.2 % offset-type value) is 709 MPa.

The Orowan strengthening contribution of the Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si test steel is 0 MPa because Al and Si additions suppress carbide formation, so no significant precipitates form and no precipitation strengthening occurs.
Retained austenite content in the ANT750 specimen is <5 % and its strengthening contribution was therefore neglected.
Average error between predicted and measured YS for the Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si alloys annealed at 750–850 °C was 1.56 % (the 750 °C ANT750 case contributes to this average).

SHAP/feature-importance analysis (Fig. 17, performed for the Fe-9.7Mn-2.04Al-0.99Si-0.52V-0.42C composition, not ANT750) ranked dislocation strengthening as the dominant contributor, followed by Orowan strengthening, then fine-grain and solid-solution strengthening.
